title: Tonal Noise from the Pack Bay Reported by the Cabin Crew in the Cruise
abstract: Fault isolation for a tonal noise reported from the pack bay in the cruise, distinguishing a genuine machine defect from the expected acoustic signature of an unmodified air cycle machine.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates a tonal noise reported from the pack bay in the cruise, and establishes whether it is a defect that requires rectification or the normal signature of an air cycle machine that has not had the tuned silencer.
sections.fault_description: Cabin crew report a whistle or whine from the rear cabin floor area in the cruise, usually at high cabin load and only above a certain machine speed. There is no flight deck indication and no maintenance message. The important distinction is between the known 3.2 kilohertz turbine tone, which is characteristic of the original silencer and is not a defect, and a broadband rumble or a rising note, which indicates a bearing problem and must be rectified.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Obtain the cabin report and record the flight phase, the cabin load and the seat rows where the noise was heard. 2. Ask the crew whether the noise was a steady whistle or a rising note, because the two have different causes. 3. Record the cabin sound level at the reported rows on the next sector with the sound level meter and capture a spectrum. 4. A single peak at 3.2 kilohertz that appears above 88 per cent machine speed is the known turbine tone: confirm whether the aircraft has the tuned silencer fitted. 5. If the aircraft has not been modified, no rectification is required and the operator should be offered the silencer retrofit. 6. If the aircraft has the tuned silencer and the tone is still present, inspect the silencer KEDE723823-59 for liner delamination. 7. A rising or wandering note indicates a bearing problem: shut the pack down and inspect the machine for free rotation. 8. Check the mount washers EN911564K9 for extrusion or set, because a collapsed mount transmits structure-borne noise that the crew hear as a rumble. 9. Check that the pipe at FIN 4HM is clipped clear of the silencer body and that the filter at FIN 312HM is secure. 10. Where nothing is found and the noise persists, remove the machine for bench examination.
sections.dispatch_note: No dispatch restriction applies to the known turbine tone. Where a rising note or a bearing noise is confirmed, the affected pack must be shut down and the aircraft dispatched under the single pack provisions, which restrict the maximum operating altitude.

type_data.fault_symptom: Tonal noise reported from the pack bay in the cruise, no flight deck indication

possible_causes.cause: Known 3.2 kilohertz turbine tone on an aircraft without the tuned silencer
Silencer liner delamination on a modified aircraft
Machine bearing degradation giving a rising note
Collapsed or extruded mount washer transmitting structure-borne noise

dispatch.dispatch_condition: No restriction for the known turbine tone; single pack operation with altitude restriction where a bearing noise is confirmed
